text:
Alex: Quick heads-up — I ran the post-rollout cache audit after the batching heuristic change and found two things: a ~6% drop in prefix-cache hit-rate for short prompts and a handful of apparent cross-tenant key collisions in the sample window. Posting logs and notes below.
Maria: Yikes. Can you attach the raw collision sample? rough timestamps are fine.
Alex: Pasting the reduced log excerpt: ```[2026-06-12T14:02:11Z] cache_lookup ok tenant=team-alpha key=0x7f3a... hit=false 
[2026-06-12T14:02:11Z] cache_store tenant=team-beta key=0x7f3a... size=1.2KB```
Sam: The key value being identical across tenant fields is bad. Do we still include tenant in the key derivation? I thought we had tenant-salt in HMAC.
Jit: We do, nominally. Current code (post-batching) does: 
```python
normalized = normalize_prefix(raw)
cache_key = truncate(hmac_sha256(cache_salt, normalized), 16)
```
But note: normalization moved earlier/later in the serving pipeline during the batching perf patch — some callers pass already-normalized prompts and others still do normalization downstream, so identical bytes might be hashed without tenant context in a few hot paths.
Maria: That explains the collisions. If tenant context is missing before HMAC, two tenants with identical normalized bytes will collide. But why the hit-rate drop?
Alex: Warmup strategy change: we switched from deterministic prefetch (per-tenant top-k prefixes) to a probabilistic sampling pre-warm to reduce burst load. That reduced warmup coverage for short, high-frequency prefixes, so more cold misses. Together the two changes amplify each other.
PerfBot: Summary metrics: prefix_hit_rate_short_prompts dropped 0.062 (baseline 0.78 -> 0.718). collision_samples=7/1000 sampled lookups.
Sam: Security angle: even with collisions, are we exposing any plaintext? Our cache entries are AES-GCM encrypted per-entry with KMS-managed key, but the cache_key is used as the lookup. If tenant derivation is omitted, one tenant could cause eviction or reuse of another tenant's encrypted blob (the blob still encrypted), leading to potential availability/denial-of-service or oracle leaks if we accidentally decrypt with wrong associated_data.
Jit: Right — current decrypt uses AEAD with associated_data=tenant_id. If an attacker manages to fetch another tenant's entry (via collision), decryption will fail because AD mismatch, so confidentiality holds. But we could still double-charge cache hits or leak timing info. Also our monitor doesn't currently track AD-mismatch decrypt failures as security incidents.
Maria: Action items I propose: 1) Immediately re-introduce tenant_context into the hot path key derivation (non-blocking patch) 2) Rotate cache_salt (low-risk) 3) Add a short-term revert to deterministic pre-warm for short prefixes 4) Add an alert for sudden short-prefix hit-rate drops (>3%) and for decrypt AD-mismatch spikes.
Alex: I'm +1 on all. I'll open the roll-forward PR for tenant_context in the hot path and a separate ops ticket for salt rotation.
Sam: I'll own the revert/pre-warm experiment and bench it. Will measure latency impact.
Jit: I'll add an audit job that fuzzes for collisions across tenant_id space and edge-normalizations. It will run nightly and output summary into infra-monitoring.
InfraBot: Created ticket INFRA-8421 (cache-salt-rotation) and MON-3098 (prefix-hitrate-alert).
Maria: Also let's add a tiny unit test around the normalization->key pipeline to assert tenant uniqueness: assert set(keys_for_same_normalized_prompt across tenants) size == num_tenants.
Alex: Good call. One more note — we should update the design doc section on caching to document ordering invariants: normalization + tenant_context MUST happen before any truncation or sampling in key pipeline. I'll draft that and link in the PR.
Sam: TL;DR: regression was emergent from two independent perf tweaks (batch normalization reorder + probabilistic warmup). Fix is straightforward but we should harden with tests, rotate salt, and add monitoring.
Maria: Thanks. If anyone finds more collision samples drop them in this thread. I'll mark this as P1 for the day. :exclamation:
Alex: dropping the PR link here when ready; thanks everyone.
